result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep old content visible, wait about 300 ms before showing a loading cue, and handle failure well with an inline banner and Retry. A is more consistent: it keeps the dimmed results throughout, explains why skeletons are wrong for filter changes, and reserves space for the error banner so nothing shifts. B is stronger on map-local cues and retry logic, but it swaps the old results for skeletons after 1.5 s, which undercuts both keeping previous results visible and avoiding layout shift. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep stale content visible, put cues near what's changing, use a roughly 300ms threshold and handle failure well with an inline banner and Retry. B is stronger on layout stability: it rules out skeletons for filter changes and keeps them only for a first load with nothing on screen, reserves space for the error banner and animates only opacity and transform. A swaps dimmed cards for skeletons after 1.5s, which partly blanks the list it says to keep visible.
